title: Seventeen remaining compliance corrections

commandmentsBaseline.changeReview: Reviewed the complete upstream delta. Brick Contract 1.22.1 adds catalogue-only installation routing and release-matched practical recipes. Published upstream recipes and executable tests were preserved, declared, compiled and re-exercised in this combined delivery; the original seventeen findings and corrections remain applicable. Other selected subject rules are unchanged.

consumerInstallation: Manual; no live manifest, lockfile, installed package, project-local documentation or Unity state was updated.

findings.title: Authoring entry points omit required foundation and operation safeguards
findings.applicability: Current first-party source and maintained tools; no live consumer migration authorized.

requirements.section: Separate readiness and ownership; Public Editor and provider contract

findings.observed: God MutationIssue only checks play/compile/import. ForgeOperations checks broader busy and running-owner state, but neither gate verifies compatible local Commandments. Settings Review/Commit and UI menu Inspect/Commit use the weaker shared authoring eligibility. Audio RequireEdit and Object Pooling asset creation check only play state. Build Forge already demonstrates the available local foundation check.
findings.impact: A direct supported authoring API can proceed without compatible local guidance or while a conflicting build/package/content operation is active. The broader ForgeOperations dispatch does cover several busy states; the gap is foundation readiness there and incomplete guards on direct owner entry points.

evidence.description: MutationIssue returns null after only two Unity-state checks.
Dispatch gate checks ForgeEditorOperations and running owner; no local foundation inspection.
Broader busy guard exists but does not inspect the local foundation.
Review routes to shared eligibility; Commit performs a fresh Review.
Commit uses fresh Inspect and its shared MenuEligibility.
RequireEdit checks only Play Mode.
CreateInStandardFolder has only an initial Application.isPlaying state check.
Existing correct foundation inspection to reuse.

findings.proposedCorrection: Use one read-only eligibility contract at each Editor/API mutation boundary, with local foundation compatibility, actual owner state and all applicable shared busy checks. Keep read-only inspection available and avoid automatic updates.
acceptanceCriteria: Missing, incompatible or unreadable local Commandments block mutation without changing assets/settings/scenes.
Compilation failure, play/build/import, disabled owner, package/content work and state drift after review produce explicit blocked results.
Ready no-code and public API workflows still succeed; ordinary inspector editing behavior and authored state remain supported.
findings.evidenceLimit: Confirmed by call-path inspection; conflicting-state execution was not reproduced in Unity during this audit.
findings.reassessment: All earlier evidence files are unchanged at the current owning commits; applicable requirements rechecked against Commandments 0.59.0.

findings.title: Settings asset creation does not fully validate its destination chain or creation result
findings.applicability: Current first-party source and maintained tools; no live consumer migration authorized.
findings.observed: ValidateAssetPath checks path text, final occupancy and metadata length. EnsureFolder returns immediately for an AssetDatabase-valid folder, recursively creates missing parents and ignores the GUID returned by CreateFolder. It does not reject reparse/case/file conflicts along the complete chain. CreateAsset records a GUID without verifying exact persisted asset identity.
findings.impact: A linked or conflicting ancestor can pass the review; a numbered replacement folder or failed asset creation can be misreported. Actual external writes or data loss have not been demonstrated.

evidence.description: Review does not validate the complete regular-directory chain.
CreateAsset records the result without persistence verification.
EnsureFolder ignores the returned folder GUID and exact path.

findings.proposedCorrection: Validate exact containment, regular ancestors, case and occupancy immediately before each creation. Resolve returned folder GUIDs to the reviewed path and verify every created asset/GUID before reporting success; report partial changes accurately.
acceptanceCriteria: Linked ancestor, case/file collision, changed destination after review and failed CreateFolder/CreateAsset are rejected in an isolated fixture.
No external write, numbered substitute, false success or deletion of unrelated content occurs.
Valid first-party paths create exact folders/assets and retain Undo, GUID identity and unrelated authored state.
findings.evidenceLimit: Source-confirmed checks and result-verification omissions; filesystem/Unity reproductions remain unverified.
findings.reassessment: All earlier evidence files are unchanged at the current owning commits; applicable requirements rechecked against Commandments 0.59.0.

findings.title: Settings writes do not protect damaged payloads or unsupported fields
findings.applicability: Current first-party behavior and maintained guides. Audit only; no consumer migration or product correction performed.
findings.observed: BrickSettingsStore.Read validates only the outer record identity and a non-null json string. Save<T> replaces that string without parsing the existing payload, and SaveJson does the same after only a starts-with-brace check on its caller-supplied payload. SetEnabled reserializes a three-field record. There is no supported-format or unknown-field guard in these paths. A valid outer record whose json value is "not JSON" can therefore be overwritten through Save<T>; unknown outer fields are not represented or preserved.
findings.impact: A supported write can erase the original damaged payload or unsupported data instead of reporting the exact file/reason and stopping. The new contract requires preservation before writes. Malformed outer JSON and wrong package identity already have checks; this finding concerns the remaining payload/format boundary.

evidence.description: Read accepts any non-null inner payload after deserializing only three envelope fields.
Save<T> overwrites the unvalidated existing payload.
SaveJson replaces the old payload without validating its supported format.
SetEnabled uses the same lossy record writer.
Write serializes the projected record, with no unknown-data preservation or write refusal.

findings.proposedCorrection: Validate the owned envelope and owner payload before configuration-dependent use and every write. Document supported fields/formats and downgrade limits. Preserve safe unknown data, otherwise refuse the write with the exact required version. Keep existing bytes and unrelated valid modules usable; provide only explicit manual repair/reset, with a clear data-loss explanation.
acceptanceCriteria: Malformed inner JSON, wrong identity, unsupported versions and incompatible values fail before writing; the original bytes are unchanged.
Unknown fields are retained through supported writes or produce an actionable write refusal.
Missing files still use fresh defaults; existing unreadable files never become missing/default settings.
One invalid module does not block unrelated valid modules; no automatic migration, backup or rollback is introduced.
findings.evidenceLimit: Source call paths confirmed; no new Unity reproduction or damaged live file was used. Unknown-field behavior is corroborated by the Unity 6000.6 JSON serialization manual.

externalReferences.title: Unity 6000.6 JSON serialization
externalReferences.supports: Fields not represented by a serialized class are ignored; reserializing that class cannot preserve those fields.

findings.assessmentLimit: Automated and scoped native evidence; any physical/input/device limitations remain explicit.

findings.title: Skipping an excluded asset leaves its naming request attached to the next asset
findings.applicability: Current first-party behavior and maintained guides. Audit only; no consumer migration or product correction performed.

requirements.section: Explicit current-assets scans and exclusions; Optional actual-sound analysis before Codex naming

findings.observed: When the queued source becomes ignored while its naming request is active, Tick waits for completion, then takes the ineligible branch before clearing _task/_input. FinishAsset dequeues the source without clearing those fields. The following asset can consume the previous source request/result and stop the scan.
findings.impact: Changing a source into a protected/ignored location can incorrectly fail an unrelated next file. Source-current checks generally prevent applying stale output, but per-asset request ownership and cleanup are incomplete.

evidence.description: An active task is checked before current source eligibility.
Ineligible source advances the queue before request fields are cleared.
FinishAsset leaves _task and _input attached when more assets remain.

findings.proposedCorrection: Give each queued asset explicit request ownership. Clear or cancel and retire its task/input before advancing after exclusion, movement, deletion or failure; ignore late results and prepare the next source independently.
acceptanceCriteria: Move/delete/ignore the source while a controlled request is pending; that result is never reused for another GUID.
The next eligible asset gets its own input, task and verified result.
Cancellation and late replies preserve source bytes and report actual remaining work.
findings.evidenceLimit: Current source confirmed and byte-identical to the historically reproduced controlled-request path. No new paid account request or Unity execution was performed.
findings.assessmentLimit: Automated and scoped native evidence; any physical/input/device limitations remain explicit.

findings.title: Audio coverage can make valid naming history fail reload
findings.applicability: Current first-party behavior and maintained guides. Audit only; no consumer migration or product correction performed.

requirements.section: Optional Codex-assisted import naming; Optional actual-sound analysis before Codex naming

findings.observed: Parse accepts a reason of up to 240 characters. Complete appends AudioCoverage after that validation without applying a final persistence bound. Restore still rejects Reason.Length greater than 240. A valid response can therefore become invalid saved history after audio coverage is appended.
findings.impact: Automatic naming pauses on reload with a malformed-history error caused by its own otherwise valid output. The earlier controlled probe grew a 190-character response into a 354-character reason.

evidence.description: Complete appends the required audio coverage after reason validation.
The model response reason bound is 240.
Restoring saved history rejects reasons over 240.

findings.proposedCorrection: Make final persisted explanation bounds consistent with complete required coverage. Preserve the full coverage separately if necessary; never silently omit sampled ranges or channels. Keep existing valid saved data supported.
acceptanceCriteria: Maximum valid reason plus full and partial audio coverage persists and reloads successfully.
Coverage, uncertainty and partial channel/range information remain visible.
Malformed externally supplied histories still fail actionably without rewriting the original.
findings.evidenceLimit: The Complete function is unchanged from the historically probed source; the restore reason bound remains 240. The historical failure is corroboration, not a fresh Unity run on this release.
findings.assessmentLimit: Automated and scoped native evidence; any physical/input/device limitations remain explicit.

findings.title: Audio downsampling sends aliased sound to analysis
findings.applicability: Current first-party behavior and maintained guides. Audit only; no consumer migration or product correction performed.

requirements.section: Optional actual-sound analysis before Codex naming

findings.observed: Encode constructs 24 kHz output by selecting a source frame for each output frame, without a low-pass filter before downsampling. For a 48 kHz source, high-frequency content above the 12 kHz output Nyquist limit folds into lower frequencies. The historical controlled Unity probe measured an 18 kHz input appearing as a strong 6 kHz output component.
findings.impact: The optional paid sound-analysis step can receive a different audible frequency than the recording contained, undermining its evidence for naming. This is signal conversion behavior, separate from unverified semantic accuracy of the remote model.

evidence.description: The encoder handles bounded excerpts and channels.
Direct source-frame selection performs unfiltered downsampling.
Selected PCM is quantized directly into the output waveform.

findings.proposedCorrection: Use a bounded resampler with appropriate anti-alias filtering before reducing sample rate. Retain stereo, excerpt coverage, timeout, cancellation and importer preservation.
acceptanceCriteria: Synthetic out-of-band tones are attenuated before 24 kHz conversion instead of folding into strong audible aliases.
In-band tones, stereo channels, short/full clips and labelled excerpts retain expected waveform and duration.
Memory/time bounds, cancellation and unchanged import settings are validated independently of live model naming accuracy.
findings.evidenceLimit: The entire encoder file is byte-identical to the historically tested source. That probe observed 6 kHz amplitude 0.4514 from an 18 kHz/48 kHz input. No listening/device or fresh Unity acceptance is claimed.
findings.assessmentLimit: Automated and scoped native evidence; any physical/input/device limitations remain explicit.

findings.title: Paused imports can display an earlier completed scan as current progress
findings.applicability: Current first-party behavior and maintained guides. Audit only; no consumer migration or product correction performed.
findings.observed: InspectRenaming/InspectReorganising select automatic import progress only when ImportProgress.Running is true. ImportProgress sets Running false when paused, even with pending files. The inspection then returns the last explicit scan, which can still show 100 percent and Completed.
findings.impact: A blocked pending import is displayed as completed work, obscuring the active failure and remaining queue.

evidence.description: The public progress API falls back to the previous explicit scan when automatic work is paused.
Paused automatic work with a pending queue is marked not running.

findings.proposedCorrection: Report the current operation, pending count and paused/failed stage independently of running status. Retain past outcomes as history without presenting them as the current queue.
acceptanceCriteria: After a completed scan, a new paused import displays its actual pending count and failure below 100 percent.
Rename and reorganisation views identify their operation and do not substitute another prior result.
Native normal/narrow boxed progress and public inspection outputs agree.
findings.evidenceLimit: Current inspected code remains equivalent to the historical controlled probe, which reported one pending import while the public progress remained 100 percent. Native rendering was not repeated.

Its opening still says Release 0.5.1 for BigBang 0.8.1, Release 0.35.0 for God 0.38.1, and Release 0.9.0 for Angels 0.9.3, then calls ForgeCapabilities.json this release's declaration. Current God guide still identifies Release 0.35.0.
Current Angels guide still identifies Release 0.9.0.
The outdated AI guide is explicitly classified as current.

Historical versions are labelled and do not imply current validation.

unverified: Physical keyboard/mouse, alternate skin, high-DPI and device acceptance were not performed. Native dark-skin Inspector captures are scoped to the recorded panels and widths.

Windows batch players validate APIs, persistence and ordinary bootstrap ownership. They do not certify visual console layout, physical input, audible output, native Steam sessions or every product capability.
FMOD has separately recorded real licensed compilation and native NOSOUND_NRT checks. Audible/device acceptance and unchanged vendor RuntimeManager behavior remain outside this correction.
Real paid model naming accuracy was not tested. Synthetic audio/filtering and controlled late/cancelled request tests do not certify semantic naming accuracy.
BigBang remains exempt from dependency compliance and dependency-driven changes. Consumer installation is manual; unfinished SaveLoad and Steam features were not implemented.

publicationPolicy.immutableGitReleases: Each owning remote main and exact fixed release commit/tag are verified. Published contents and tags were preserved; no release tag was moved or replaced.
publicationPolicy.githubReleaseLock: The additional GitHub lock flag is observed per repository in each publication record. SaveLoad has it disabled; repository settings were not changed. Archive and checksum digests were independently verified for every release.
